name: Stormwind (kingdom)
summary: In the years after Lordaeron fell, Stormwind is the Alliance's foremost power and humanity's greatest remaining bastion. Its southern lands include Elwynn Forest, Westfall, Duskwood, and the Redridge Mountains. Sacked in the First War and rebuilt after the Second, the kingdom now has a ten-year-old king, Anduin Wrynn, while Highlord Bolvar Fordragon guides its affairs amid troubles at home and beyond its borders.

sections.title: A Legacy of Defiance
sections.body: Stormwind began more than a thousand years ago, founded by descendants of the ancient Arathi empire. They traveled south beyond the crags of Khaz Modan into fertile, forested valleys. Far from the northern kingdoms, Stormwind grew proud of its self-reliance and its faith in the Light.

sections.title: Ashes and Restoration
sections.body:
The Orcish Horde came through the Dark Portal, and Stormwind's independence neared its end. In the First War, Stormwind City burned to ash and King Llane was slain. Sir Anduin Lothar led the survivors north across the Great Sea, where he rallied the northern realms into the Alliance of Lordaeron.

After the Orcish threat was crushed in the Second War, refugees returned. They hired the Stonemasons Guild to rebuild their capital with white stone and blue banners. Then the Scourge wiped out Lordaeron during the Third War, leaving Stormwind humanity's greatest remaining bastion.

sections.title: A Fractured Realm
sections.body:
Stormwind struggles to govern its vast southern holdings. Elwynn Forest remains relatively secure, but outlaws swarm through Westfall, while orcs and gnolls repeatedly enter Redridge. Duskwood's darkened woods have slipped from the kingdom's control.

A bitter dispute between the House of Nobles and the Stonemasons erupted into violent riots in the capital. Displaced workers took up open rebellion across the provinces.

sections.title: The Hollow Throne
sections.body:
King Varian Wrynn disappeared while sailing to a diplomatic summit with the Horde at Theramore. His ten-year-old son, Anduin Wrynn, inherited the crown, and Highlord Bolvar Fordragon became Lord Regent to preserve fragile public order.

Royal authority remains divided and stalled. Guided closely by the enigmatic Lady Katrana Prestor, the House of Nobles repeatedly vetoes military deployments. Local towns must defend themselves as dangerous secrets fester within Stormwind Keep.

faq.answer: King Anduin Wrynn holds Stormwind's crown, while Highlord Bolvar Fordragon governs as Lord Regent because the king is a child. Lady Katrana Prestor and the House of Nobles provide heavy counsel and oversight.

faq.q: What happened to King Varian Wrynn?
faq.answer: King Varian Wrynn left Stormwind on a confidential diplomatic voyage to Theramore to negotiate peaceful relations with the Horde. He vanished along the way, and his fate remains a guarded state secret, kept from the kingdom's people and external rivals to prevent chaos.

faq.q: Why was Stormwind destroyed in the past?
faq.answer: The Orcish Horde first encountered a human nation when it invaded Stormwind through the Dark Portal in the First War. King Llane and Sir Anduin Lothar led a stubborn defense, but the city was breached, sacked, and razed. The survivors fled north by sea to Lordaeron.

faq.q: Why are Westfall, Redridge, and Duskwood lacking royal soldiers?
faq.answer: Court politics and a stretched royal military leave Westfall, Redridge, and Duskwood without royal soldiers. Lady Katrana Prestor and the House of Nobles often block requests for garrisons beyond Elwynn Forest, arguing that capital funds and forces cannot be spent policing peripheral lands. The People's Militia and the Night Watch are left to fight alone.

faq.q: What territory does the Kingdom of Stormwind claim?
faq.answer: Stormwind claims Elwynn Forest, the Redridge Mountains, Westfall, and Duskwood on Azeroth's southern continent. It once maintained frontier posts reaching south into northern Stranglethorn Vale.

faq.q: Why did the Stonemasons turn against Stormwind?
faq.answer: After rebuilding Stormwind City in white stone, the Stonemasons Guild presented its invoice. Influenced by noble politics, the House of Nobles refused full payment, and the stonemasons would not compromise. Riots followed, driving the guild out to become the outlaw Defias Brotherhood.

angles.text: As a human, you stand with Stormwind, humanity's beating heart and last sovereign stronghold after Lordaeron, Alterac, and Dalaran fell in the north.
As an Alliance member, you look to Stormwind as the Alliance's main military and economic anchor. It offers shelter, leadership, and resources to its dwarven, gnomish, and night elven allies.
As a paladin, you follow the ancient holy traditions of the Church of the Holy Light and the legacy of the Silver Hand. The Cathedral of Light houses consecrated orders.
As a rogue, you know Stormwind's bitter domestic strife and the Defias uprising have filled its back alleys, sewers, and countryside with opportunistic cutpurses and political spies.
